title: Four-rule iPRA with reusable clauses
mathematical_claims: Four inference schemes (Use, Step, Open, Close) plus one fixed universal-reflexivity clause.
Exact public consequence equivalence with the pinned five-pattern zero-normal clause calculus, by effective proof translations.
The ordinary realization is bi-interpretable and equiconsistent with full first-order intuitionistic primitive recursive arithmetic.
Both numerical interpretation domains are whole, equality is actual equality, and both composite numerical isomorphisms have graph x=y.
Both formula composites are provably equivalent to the original formula.
The packet checker is sound and complete for closed native theorems, under the usual sufficient-resource convention.
limits: Reflexivity is relocated to a fixed counted axiom clause, not derived from Step alone.
Most size savings come from the proof protocol and data representation; clause factorization alone has a modest measured effect.
No absolute minimum or new global compact-checker record is claimed.
The historical 516-byte compact and 788-byte public-goal validated profiles are not beaten.
Rank flattening alone is not the best measured representation.
The support-derived-rank quotient is unselected because its checker is larger.
New results have written proofs and executable tests, not a Lean or Rocq formalization.
Inherited Lean sources were inspected but not rebuilt during this run.
Finite test success is not a proof of consistency or of the universal interpretation theorem.
